method: Direct Codex authored outputs, one reviewer, three varied fixtures; not independent stochastic runs.

fixtures.input: We launched the product last month and are seeing great results. Users report high satisfaction.
fixtures.actual_output: No tense correction required: the launch is a completed past event, while results and reports continue in the present. The qualitative claims need evidence only if the document requires substantiation.
fixtures.check: Preserves legitimate temporal distinction; adds no facts.

fixtures.input: Our product is the best on the market because customers love it.
fixtures.actual_output: Logic: customer affection alone does not establish market leadership. Ask for comparative evidence, or soften to “Customers have responded positively” only if the stated feedback supports that. Do not add ratings or market share.

fixtures.input: The feature launched in Q3, so adoption increased.
fixtures.actual_output: Logic: “so” asserts causation not established by timing alone. Suggested fix: “The feature launched in Q3; adoption subsequently increased.” Ask for supporting causal evidence before attributing the increase to the launch.
